sentences.text: Earth's rotation axis is tilted twenty-three and a half degrees to its orbital plane and points the same way all year.
At the December solstice the South Pole leans toward the Sun and the North Pole away from it: the day-night line cuts across Earth at its steepest angle.
Beyond the Arctic Circle the Sun never rises; in the south, Antarctica is lit by the midnight sun.
Seen from orbit, Earth reaches this point of its journey around the Sun every year on 21–22 December.
It is this tilt, not distance, that makes the seasons: Earth actually passes closest to the Sun in early January.
